transcript:
User: Yeah, I got a voicemail from you people. This better be quick, I've got three jobs waiting.
Agent: Got it—you got our voicemail, and I’ll keep it quick. What caught your attention in the message?
User: You wanted to discuss some savings on insurance. Everyone says that, so what's the deal here?
Agent: Yeah, totally fair—“savings on insurance” gets thrown around a lot. Before I explain, what kind of business are you running?
User: That's none of your business. I'm here to see if this is worth my time, not chat.
Agent: I hear you. In plain terms, we stop you losing money from missed calls by answering, qualifying, and booking jobs—so you’re not stuck playing phone tag. What’s happening right now when someone calls and you can’t pick up?
User: I miss calls, sure. But how do I know this isn't just some scam? Everyone promises the world.
Agent: Makes sense to be cautious. What would you need to see to feel confident it’s legit—real call recordings, a short live demo, or references from businesses like yours?
User: I don't need more sales pitches. Just tell me how this is different from all the others.
Agent: Got it. The difference is we tie it to one outcome: missed calls get answered and turned into booked jobs—then you can verify it with real call logs/recordings, not vague “savings” claims. Which matters more to you to prove it fast: seeing actual call results, or hearing a quick live demo on a real missed-call scenario?
User: Neither. I don't trust any of that. Why do you need to see my call logs anyway?
Agent: Totally get that— and we don’t need your call logs to talk; logs are only optional if you want to measure how many calls you’re missing and what that’s costing you. Roughly how many calls a week do you think hit voicemail when you’re on jobs?
User: That's none of your business. I'm not sharing numbers with you. What's the catch here?
Agent: Got it—no numbers. There isn’t a catch: you don’t have to share call logs, and you can keep control of what the caller hears and when it hands off to you; if it’s not recovering missed-call revenue, you don’t keep it. When calls go to voicemail, do those people usually leave a message—or just call the next company?
User: Most just hang up. But I'm not convinced this will change anything. Why should I believe you?
Agent: Yeah—if most hang up, that’s exactly where money slips away. What would you consider “proof” that it’s working—more booked jobs showing up on your calendar, or fewer missed calls going to voicemail?
User: Everyone says they'll fix the missed calls. Show me something real, not just empty promises.
Agent: Totally fair—real proof is results, not talk. If we could show you a few actual call outcomes (missed call → answered → job booked) using a test number without touching your call logs, would you be open to that?
User: Fine, as long as it's quick and doesn't mess with my current setup. But I'm still skeptical.
Agent: Totally fair—and we can keep it quick, and it won’t replace your current setup; it can just catch the calls you’re missing and hand off when needed. When a caller hangs up, what’s the most common thing they’re calling you for—pricing, scheduling, or an emergency job?
User: Probably emergencies, but why do you need to know that? Just get to the point, already.
Agent: Got it—emergencies matter because the call flow has to prioritize those and get the right details fast so you can dispatch without back-and-forth. When an emergency call comes in and you miss it, what’s the usual outcome—do they call someone else, or do they eventually call back?
User: They might call someone else. But I don't see how you can help with that.
Agent: Makes sense—if they call someone else, it’s usually because nobody answered in the moment. We help by answering those emergency calls right away, grabbing the key details, and either booking it or getting it to you fast without changing your current phone setup.  

When an emergency call comes in, what’s the one detail you always need first—address, issue, or availability?
User: Look, I just need to know what the problem is. But I still don't see how you help.
Agent: Got it. The problem is simple: when you’re on jobs, emergency callers hang up and book the next company—so you lose jobs you would’ve won if someone answered right then.  

Has anyone ever shown you the math on what that’s costing you?
User: That's none of your business. I don't need math to tell me I'm losing money. Everyone says that.
Agent: Makes sense—you don’t need a spreadsheet to feel it. If we could stop emergency callers from hanging up by answering instantly and capturing the details, would that be worth exploring?
User: Everyone says they can do that. What's your guarantee? If this wastes my time, I'm done.
Agent: Totally fair—if it wastes your time, you should be done. The only “guarantee” I can give on this call is we can run it in a way that doesn’t change your current setup, and you’ll be able to judge it by real outcomes (answered missed calls and booked jobs) before you commit.  

What would you count as a clear win in the first week—one extra booked emergency job, or just seeing missed calls get answered?
User: I've heard this before. Show me one extra booked job, or it's a waste. Now, I'm done.
Agent: Got it—one extra booked job is the bar. Real quick—if I could guarantee you 5 to 10 extra booked jobs in your first month, would it be worth 20 minutes to see exactly how we’d do it?
User: No, I've heard it all before. I don't have time for this. Bye.
Agent: Got it—thanks for the time. If you ever want to revisit stopping those missed emergency calls from going to competitors, give us a call back. Take care.
